and Pellets

FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Ores and Raw Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division 
Council. 


This standard was first published in 1984 and then subsequently revised in 1994. With the experience gained by 
the Committee over time and changes in technical requirements in the field, the Committee has decided to revise 
this standard and has made following changes in Section 2 ‘Static Reduction Degradation (RDI) test’ of this 
Indian Standard to harmonize it with ISO 4696 which had been revised recently: 


a) Testing temperature, 

b) Mesh apertures of sieves to be used, 

c) Clause ‘Sampling and Sample Preparation’ has been modified, and 

d) Sub clauses ‘Reduction’ and ‘Tumbling’ under clause ‘Procedure’ have been modified. 


This test method is now technically equivalent to that specified in ISO 4696-2 : 2015 which would facilitate 
evaluation of Indian Iron ores as per International Standards. 


It is well known that iron ore and its agglomerates, namely, sinter and pellets, henceforth called ‘iron bearing 
materials’, undergo size degradation as a result of thermal shock as well as phase changes coupled with thermal 
stresses during reduction at elevated temperatures. The extent to which a particular type of ore or its agglomerates 
undergo degradation, if known to the blast furnace operator, helps to a great extent in the selection of the blast 
furnace burden. 


This standard is one of a series of standards on the methods for determination of various characteristics of iron 
ores and its agglomerates and it lays down the methods for determination of the extent of degradation under 
thermal shock or under thermal shock combined with reduction reaction. Since the burden inside the blast furnace 
is constantly moving downwards while the iron bearing materials are simultaneously getting reduced, the extent 
of degradation may be measured in the following two ways: (a) Thermal Degradation Index (TDI), that is the 
effect of thermal shock on the degradation behaviour of iron bearing materials, and (b) Reduction Degradation 
Index (RDI), that is degradation due to chemical changes which occur. 


For determining these properties, tests may be done under ‘static’ conditions and then the sample may be tumbled 
in cold condition after the test is over or else the sample itself may be placed in a rotating bomb (dynamic) while 
the heating and reduction is in progress. 


In the formulation of this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO 4696-2 : 2015 ‘Iron ores for blast 
furnace feedstocks — Determination of low-temperature reduction-disintegration indices by static method — 
Part 2: Reduction with CO and N,' issued by the International Organization for Standardization’ (ISO). 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (revised)’. 


IS 10823 : 2018 


Indian Standard 


METHODS FOR DETERMINATION OF THERMAL 
DEGRADATION INDEX (TDI) AND REDUCTION 
DEGRADATION INDEX (RDI) OF IRON OXIDES; LUMP 
ORES, SINTER AND PELLETS 


(Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies the methods to be followed 
for the determination of the degradation index of iron 
oxides’ lump ores, sinter and pellets. Section 1 and 
Section 2 of this standard prescribe method for the 
determination for degradation index under static bed 
followed by cold tumbling whereas Section 3 of this 
standard prescribes the method for the determination 
for degradation index during tumbling. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given below contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. Allstandards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of these standards. 


IS No. Title 
460 Specification for test sieves: 
(Part 1): 1985 Wire cloth test sieves (third revision) 
(Part 2): 1985 Perforated plate test sieves (third 
revision)

Preparation manual method (third 
revision) 

1607 : 2013 Methods for test sieving (second 
revision) 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply: 


3.2 Degradation — The tendency of the iron bearing 
materials to undergo size degradation as a result of 
either thermal shock or reduction or both. The term 
‘Decrepitation’ or ‘Low Temperature Breakdown 
(LTB)’ are also used in the place of Degradation in 
technical literature. However, ‘Degradation’ is used in 
this standard for clarity. 


3.3 Thermal Degradation — The degradation of the 
iron bearing materials under normal atmosphere 
because of thermal shock. 


3.4 Reduction Degradation — The degradation of the 
iron bearing materials because of reduction and related 
stresses introduced in the matrix due to phase changes. 


SECTION 1 STATIC THERMAL 
DEGRADATION TEST (TDI) 


4 PRINCIPLE OF TEST 


4.1 To evaluate the effect of rapid heating from room 
temperature to 600°C in 30 min on sized test portion. 
This is done by measuring the mass of material passing 
a 6.3 mm screen after the heating cycle. 


4.2 The sample is placed in a sample holder which is 
then covered. The holder with the sample is then 
inserted into a furnace and heated either in normal or 
reducing atmosphere as the case may be for a given 
period of time. After that the sample is removed from 
the furnace and cooled to room temperature. Then by a 
mechanical treatment similar in principle to a tumbler 
test, the weak particles are disintegrated. The sample 
is then screened to determine the Degradation Index. 


5 APPARATUS 


5.1 Furnace — An electrically heated furnace with 
heating capacity and thermal response characteristics 
sufficient to heat the sample from room temperature to 
700°C in 30 min. 


The furnace is to be equipped with a control device so 
that the heating rate of the sample can be regulated. 


5.2 Sample Holder — The sample holder shall be made 
from heat resisting steel or material (like INCONEL 600) 
equipped with a thermocouple to measure the temperature 
of the sample. The cover shall be of the loose fitting type 
and shall not provide a gas-tight seal (see Fig. 1). 


5.3 Sieves — Test sieves, having square mesh aperture 
of 25.0 mm, 20.0 mm, 10.0 mm, 6.3 mm, 3.15 mm and 
500 um. 


6 SAMPLING 


The test sample shall be prepared according to IS 1405 
from the sample for physical testing. A quantity of

450

FURNACE

sample sufficient to provide at least ten 500 g test 
portions shall be prepared. 


Screen the sample on 12.5 mm and 10.0 mm sieves 
and after sieving, this material shall be oven dried at 
105 + 5°C for at least 2 h. 


After drying, the test materials shall be kept in 
desiccator until testing and only particles taken at 
random shall be used to constitute a test portion. 


7 TEST CONDITIONS 


The sample container shall be placed into the furnace 
held at 600°C. After the temperature of the container 
reaches 600°C, it shall be held for further 30 min. 


8 PROCEDURE FOR STATIC THERMAL 
DEGRADATION TEST (TDD 


8.1 Mass 


Weigh approximately 500 g (+ 1 particle) of the pre- 
dried test sample (mass mọ). 


8.2 Heating 


Begin heating the furnace, when the furnace temperature 
has reached 600°C. Introduce the sample holder 
alongwith the sample into the furnace. Wait for the 
charged bed to reach 600°C. The test begins at this point 
and it continues for 30 min. After 30 min remove sample 


and container from furnace and cool to room temperature. 
Discharge the sample carefully from the container and 
determine its mass (mass m,). The sample shall be 
tumbled for 30 min at 30 rpm. The size of the tumbler 
vessel shall be 130 mm x 200 mm. Hand sieve with care 
on 10.0 mm, 6.3 mm, 3.15 mm and 500 um screens. 


Mechanical sieving may be used provided that 
preliminary tests give results similar to those obtained 
by hand sieving, within the permissible tolerance of 
2 percent absolute. 
NOTE — It is considered that the set of sieves used for sieving 
should include a sieve of suitable aperture size between 10.0 
mm and 6.3 mm (for example 8.3 mm) in order to improve the 


efficiency of the 6.3 mm sieve by decreasing the sample mass 
retained on it. 


Determine and record the masses of the +10.0 mm, 
—6.3 mm, —3.15 mm and —500 um fractions. 


9 EXPRESSIONS AND RESULTS 


9.1 Calculation of the TDI 


The thermal degradation index, TDI expresses as a 
percentage by mass, is calculated from the following 
formula to one decimal place: 


M, 
TDI - 6.3 = x 100 
m 


1 


where 
m, = mass of the test portion after the thermal 
treatment, and 
m, = mass of —6.3 mm fraction obtained after 


screening. 


The mass percent passing 3.15 mm and 500 um shall 
also be reported. 


9.2 Number of Tests 


Because of the heterogeneity of natural ores the test 
shall be carried out five times and the mean value of 
the individual results to be reported as Ore Thermal 
Degradation Index. 


10 TEST REPORT 
The test report shall include the following information: 


a) Reference to this Indian Standard; 

b) Details necessary for the identification of the 
sample; 

c) The individual results of the five tests shall 
be reported; 

d) Reference number of results;and 


e) Any characteristics noticed during the test and 
any operations, which may had an influence 
on the results; for example, sampling point, 
scalping sieves used;method of sieving, loss 
of mass during the test. 


SECTION 2 STATIC REDUCTION 
DEGRADATION TEST (RDI) 
11 PRINCIPLE 


The test portion is isothermally reduced in a fixed bed, 
at 550 °C, using a reducing gas consisting of CO and 
N,, for 30 min. The reduced test portion is tumbled in 
a specific tumble drum for 900 revolutions and then 
sieved with a sieve having square openings of 2.80 mm. 
The reduction-disintegration index (RDI) is calculated 
as the mass percentage of material of — 2.80 mm. 


12 TEST CONDITIONS 


Gas volumes and flow rates are as measured at a 
temperature of 0°C and at atmospheric pressure. 


12.1 Composition of Reducing Gas 
The reducing gas shall consist of: 
CO = 30+ 0.5 percent 
N, = 70+0.5 percent 
Impurities in the reducing gas shall not exceed 
H, = 0.02% (v/v) 
O, 0.1% (v/v) 
H,O = 0.2% (v%) 


IS 10823 : 2018 


Significantly different reduction degradation indices, 
however, can be obtained when the reducing gas 
contains 2 percent hydrogen rather than less than 
0.02 percent hydrogen. 


12.2 Flow Rate of Reducing Gas 


The reducing gas flow rate shall, during the test period, 
be maintained at 20 + 1 l/min. 


12.3 Temperature of Test 


The reducing gas shall be preheated before entering 
the test portion to maintain the test portion at 
550 + 10°C during the entire test period. 


13 APPARATUS 
The apparatus shall consist of the following (see Fig. 2): 


a) asystem to supply and regulate the gases; 
b) areduction tube; 


c) an electrically heated furnace to heat the 
sample to the specified temperature; 


d) atumbler drum; 
e) test sieves; and 
f) aweighing device. 
13.1 Reduction Tube 
Made of non-scaling, heat-resistant metal to withstand 


a temperature of greater than 600°C. The diameter of 
the sample bed shall be 75 + 1 mm. 


The test portion may be placed on a perforated plate 
or, if desired, on alumina balls on the perforated plate, 
in order to ensure a uniform gas flow through the test 
portion (see Fig. 3). 


13.2 Furnace 


Having a heating capacity sufficient to maintain the 
entire test portion and the gas entering the bed at 550 + 
10°C and being equipped with a heating element 
suitable for the specified temperature. 


13.3 Tumbler Drum 


Consisting of a vessel having an internal diameter of 
130 mm and an inside length of 200 mm. 


Two equally spaced steel lifters 200 mm long and 20 mm 
wide and 2 mm thick shall be mounted longitudinally 
inside the drum. These may be mounted on a frame that 
can be inserted inside the vessel from the end. 


One end of the vessel shall be closed and the other 
open. A close fitting lid shall be held in place on the 
opening to ensure a dust tight seal (see Fig. 4). 


13.4 Test Sieves 


Having square mesh apertures of the following nominal 
Sizes:

16.0 mm, 12.5 mm, 10.0 mm, 6.3 mm, 2.8 mm

13.5 Weighing Device 


Adequate load capacity and accurate to 0.1 g. 


14 SAMPLING AND SAMPLE PREPARATION 


The test sample shall be prepared in accordance to 
IS 1405, from the sample for Physical Testing. 


14.1 Lump Iron Ore or Sinter 


The size range for sinters and lump ores shall be 
—20.0 mm to + 16.0 mm and shall be prepared as follows: 


Screen the sample on 20.0 mm sieve and carefully crush 
the +20.0 mm material until it all passes the 22.4 mm 
sieve. Combine all the fractions and remove, by sieving, 
the +20.0 mm and —16.0 mm material from the sample. 
A test sample of at least 2 kg, on dry basis, of the sized 
material shall be obtained. 


14.2 Pellets 
The size range for pellets shall be— 12.5 mm to + 10.0 mm. 


14.3 Preparation of Test Samples 


Collect each test portion by taking ore particles at 
random. Oven-dry the test sample to constant mass at 
105°C + 5°C and cool it to room temperature before 
preparation of the test portions. At least 4 test portions, 
each of approximately 500 g (+ the mass of 1 particle) 
shall be prepared from the test sample. Weigh the test 
portions to the nearest 0.1 g and register the mass of 
each test portion. 


15 PROCEDURE 


15.1 Number of Determinations 
Carry out the test generally in duplicate 
15.2 Test Portion 


Weigh to the nearest 0.1 g, approximately 500 g 
(+ 1 particle) of the test sample. The test portion should

be obtained from the test sample either by means of 
riffle divider or by manual increment division method. 


15.3 Reduction 


Place the test portion (15.2) in the reduction tube (13.1) 
so that the surface is even. Close the top of the reduction 
tube. Then insert the reduction tube into the furnace 
(13.2) and, if desired, attach it to the weighing device 
of appropriate capacity and accuracy (13.5), ensuring 
that there is no contact with the furnace or heating 
elements. 


Replace the air in the tube with inert gas. Heat the test 
portion and while heating pass a flow of inert 
gas [N,gas] through the test portion at flow rate of 
approximately 5 l/min. Continue the heating, while 
passing the inert gas until the test portion reaches the 
test temperature of 550 + 10°C and 15 l/min during 
temperature- equilibration period. During cooling, it 
shall be maintained at 5 l/min. 


NOTE — Unless the characteristics of the furnace and 
thermocouple are very well known a period of about 15 min 
should be allowed for temperature equilibration at 550°C. 


CAUTION — Carbon monoxide and the reducing gas which 
contains carbon monoxide are toxic and therefore hazardous. 
The reduction shall be carried out in a well ventilated area or 
under a hood. Precautions shall be taken for the safety of the 
operator. 


Introduce the reducing gas (12.1) ata flow rate of 15+ 1 
l/min to replace the inert gas to reduce the test portion. 
Continue the reduction with the reducing gas for 30 min. 


After 30 min reduction time, stop the flow of the reducing 
gas and cool the test portion, to a temperature below 
100°C in the reduction tube under the flow of inert gas. 


15.4 Tumbling 


Remove the test portion carefully from the reduction 
tube, determine the mass (mass mọ) and place it in the 
tumbler drum (13.3). Fasten the lid tightly and rotate 
the drum for a total of 900 revolutions at a rate of 
30 + 1 rev/min. 


Remove all material from the drum, determine the mass, 
hand sieve with care on 6.3 mm, 2.80 mm and 500 um 
sieves. Determine and record the mass of each fraction 
retained on 6.3 mm (mass m,), 2.80 mm (mass m,) and 
500 um (mass m,). Material lost during tumbling and 
sieving shall be considered to be minus 500 um. 
NOTE — Mechanical sieving may be used provided that 


preliminary test results give similar results to hand sieving 
within the permissible tolerance of 2 percent absolute. 


16 EXPRESSION OF RESULTS 


The reduction disintegration index, RDI as a percentage 
by mass, is calculated by the following formula : 


m. — (im +m) i00 


RDI - (2.8) = 


where 
My) = mass in grams of test portion after reduction 
and before tumbling, 
m, = mass in grams of oversize fraction retained 
on the 6.3 mm sieve, and 
m, = mass in grams of oversize fractions retained 


on the 2.8 mm sieve. 
17 TEST REPORT 
The test report shall include the following information: 


a) Reference to this standard; 


b) Results of the test, reduction — disintegration 
indices expressed to one decimal place; 

c) Identification of the sample; 

d) Reducing gas composition used; 

e) Sieving conditions: method of sieving, and 
sieving time; 

f) Total mass of material inserted into the tumbler 
drum and taken from tumbler drum; and 

g) Any operation and any test conditions not 
specified in this standard or regarded as 
optional which may have had an influence on 
the results. 


SECTION 3 DYNAMIC DEGRADATION TEST 


18 PRINCIPLE OF TEST 


The sample is placed in a sample holder (barrel) which 
can rotate and give a mechanical treatment similar in 
principle to a tumbler test. The holder(barrel) with a 
sample is then inserted into a furnace is then heated either 
in normal or reducing atmosphere as the case may be for 
a given period of time. After the test, the sample is removed 
from the furnace and cooled to room temperature. The 
sample is then sized to determine the Degradation Index. 


19 SAMPLE 


The sample in the size range of —12.5 mm to 10.0 mm 
and the quantity of 500 + 1g drawn as per the method 
given in IS 1405 dried at 105 + 5°C for 2h shall be 
selected for the purpose of this test. 


20 APPARATUS 


20.1 Furnace 


An electrically heated furnace with heating capacity 
and thermal response characteristics sufficient to heat 
the sample and holder to 600°C in 60 min. 


20.2 Sample Holder 


A sketch of sample holder barrel is given in Fig. 5. 
This barrel is 200 mm in length and 130 mm internal 
diameter in its central portion which holds the sample. 
This portion has 4 equally spaced 200 mm x 20 mm 


lifters mounted on its inside face. The barrel tapers on 
its both ends to 50 mm internal diameter in 75 mm 
length. The ends of the barrel are provided with 
arrangements for rotating it at 10 rpm and for gas flow 
through this. 


20.3 Sieves 


Sieves shall be of the square mesh type and shall 
conform to the requirements given in IS 460 (Part 1) 
or IS 460 (Part 2). 


21 PROCEDURE 


21.1 Dry the sample till a constant mass is reached. 
Then place the sample in the sample holder barrel at 
room temperature. 


21.2 For Dynamic Thermal Degradation Test 
(TDI) dynamic 

Place the barrel with the furnace which has been 
preheated 550+ 10°C and start the rotation of the barrel 
at 10 + 0.5 rev/min. After the sample has attained 
550°C, soak it for 60 min at this temperature. 


21.3 For Dynamic Reduction Degradation Test 
(RDI) dynamic 


Place the barrel containing the sample in the furnace at 
room temperature and start rotating it at 10 + 0.5 rev/ 
min and put on the furnace and raise the temperature of 
sample at the rate of 10°C per minute to 550 + 10°C and 
soak it for 10 min under neutral atmosphere (by passing 
nitrogen gas at a rate of about 3 litres per minute through 
the barrel from the time the barrel starts rotating). Then 
pass gas mixture of 30 percent carbon monoxide and 


GAS 
OUTLET 


a 


200 


IS 10823 : 2018 


70 percent nitrogen at the rate of 15 litres per min for 1 
h maintaining the sample temperature at 550 + 10°C. 
Then cool the sample to 350°C under neutralatmosphere 
(by passing nitrogen gas at the rate of about 3 litres per 
minute in the barrel) by putting off the furnace. Then 
take out the barrel and cool it to room temperature. 


21.4 Take out the sample and weigh the sample to an 
accuracy of 0.1g. Sieve the sample according to 
IS 1607. Determine the mass of each of the fractions to 
the nearest 0.1g. 


21.5 The Dynamic Thermal Degradation Index 
(TDI) gynamic Of Dynamic Reduction Degradation Index 
(RDD dynamic 18 expressed as the percentage of— 3.15 mm 
fraction generated after tumbling. 


21.6 Indices for other screen sizes (6.3 mm, —5.0 mm, 
—1.00 mm or 500 um) may also be reported since this 
data shall be collected in any case. 


21.7 Number of Tests 


At least two tests shall be carried out and the individual 
as well as the average values reported. 


22 TEST REPORT 
The test report shall contain the following information: 


a) Identification of the sample; 


b) Initial and final mass of the sample before and 
after the test; 


c) Degradation Index for each test and the mean; 
and 


d) Reference to this Indian Standard. 


50 ID 


All dimensions in millimetres.
